title: Startup cache seeding and weight staging for fast dedicated node readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated nodes often incur 2–10x higher tail latency and throughput drops during model load and cold KV cache misses after scale events. This ticket implements a two-tier warm strategy that stages model weights into GPU memory in a lightweight mapping step and pre-seeds KV caches using representative request traces to reduce cold-starts and meet throughput guarantees. Goals: 1) reduce P95 token latency on cold nodes by >=40% for 90% of traffic patterns; 2) reach committed throughput target within 60s of a scale-up event for common 2–4k RPS workload shapes; 3) keep additional steady-state cost overhead <8% for warm pool capacity activities.
acceptance_criteria: New warm staging flow successfully loads model weight mappings (lazy mapped pages) for v2/v3 model families and reports readiness within <35s on p4d nodes under synthetic startup test
KV-cache synthetic seeding reduces first-minute miss rate by >=60% for chat workloads (measured on trace-replay harness)
Autoscaler unit tests and e2e canary show dedicated pool reaches target throughput (<60s) for 75%+ of sampled customer workload shapes
No regressions in memory safety or node stability (zero new OOMs in canary cluster for 48h)
Rollout flag gated behind feature-flag and observable in console (per-pool warm status and cost delta)
Design doc and runbook published, and on-call briefed before production rollout
design_decisions: Two-tier warm pool: micro-warm (weight-mapped, no full init) and full-warm (weights resident + KV seeded). Tradeoff: micro-warm achieves faster readiness but may need a short additional on-demand layer init under extreme sequences.
Use OS-level demand paging + custom 'layer map' metadata instead of full eager tensor deserialize to reduce I/O footprint during staging on NFS-backed storage.
KV priming uses sampled distributed traces combined with synthetic prefix expansion to avoid seeding low-value keys - balanced for cost vs hit-rate.
Autoscaler integration prefers prefilling nodes before they enter LB pool; if prefilling fails, fallback to conservative routing with circuit-breaker to prevent SLO impact.
Expose warm state and cost impact in Console per-pool. Customers can opt-out or set max warm cost as percent of committed spend.
implementation_notes: Runtime changes: add 'stage_weights' RPC that performs memory-map reservations and verifies layer offsets without full deserialization.
Controller changes: orchestrate two warm states, track metrics (weight_mapped, kv_seeded, ready_for_traffic) and enforce SLA timers.
KV seeding harness: implement replay tool to generate prioritized key lists based on request-weighted frequency windows (configurable window size).
Metrics to emit: warm_state_transition_time, kv_seed_hit_rate_first_min, p95_token_latency_after_scale, extra_warm_cost_cents_per_hour
Failure mode: if mapping verifies but subsequent eager page fault rate is high, mark node as degraded and schedule asynchronous full-warm; reason logged to Sentry and shown in pool dashboard.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature-flagged canary in dev cluster; synthetic load test to validate mapping VM/RAM behavior (owners: Carlos, Morgan)
Week 2: Internal dedicated cluster canary (10% warm nodes). Monitor throughput readiness and memory stability for 48h. If kv_seeded hit-rate < 50% revert seed policy to micro-warm-only.
Week 3: Controlled customer pilot with opt-in pools (select customers with production traffic shapes and SRE oversight)
Week 4: Gradual ramp to 50% of new reserved capacity creation flow; add Console toggle for customers to enable warm seeding per-pool
Final: Full rollout gated on meeting acceptance criteria and post-pilot incident review
testing_plan: Unit tests for stage_weights RPC and mapping verification logic
Integration tests: drive node lifecycle through controller to validate transitions micro-warm -> full-warm
Load tests: replay 10 representative customer traces (chat, summarization, embeddings mix) and measure P95/P99 latency on scale-up
Chaos test: simulate slow NFS reads and verify fallback to conservative routing and no SLA breach
Cost regression test: estimate steady-state warm cost over a 7-day simulation and assert <8% overhead
monitoring_playbook: Primary dashboards: per-pool warm_state counts, kv_seed_hit_rate_first_min, time_to_throughput_target, weight_map_verify_failures
Alert thresholds: kv_seed_hit_rate_first_min < 40% for 5m; time_to_throughput_target > 120s for multiple nodes in same pool; weight_map_verify_failures rate > 0.5%
On-call runbook: 1) identify pool and check mapping/logs; 2) trigger async full-warm for affected nodes; 3) rollback autoscaler policy if persistent; 4) open incident if customer impact detected
Post-incident actions: capture traces, adjust seeding heuristics, and notify product support with remediation steps

notes: This ticket intentionally avoids eager weight load for all nodes to constrain sustained cost. If workloads show high sequential lengths or consistent full-model usage, the autoscaler policy may prefer full-warm nodes as default.
Consider follow-up ticket to add hardware-aware staging ordering (prioritize head layers for chat workloads).
Cross-team: coordinate with product-management for customer communication and with billing for warm-cost attribution changes.
